payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the image provide enough evidence to determine whether the paper has been stuffed into the cup?
node.criteria: Pass if the image clearly resolves whether the paper is inside the cup and stuffed into it. Fail if the image clearly shows it is not stuffed into the cup. Unknown if visibility or ambiguity prevents a determination; retain this as unresolved rather than inferring completion or absence.
node.binding: Use only visible evidence of the paper’s placement relative to the cup; do not treat proximity or contact with the rim alone as proof of stuffing.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows the paper held over the cup, with no visible portion of the paper inside it; it is not stuffed into the cup.

dependencies.evidence: The edited image shows a hand holding the paper over a cup, but the paper is not visibly inside or stuffed into it.

fulfillment: The node’s current absent judgment is not supported by the supplied edited image: it shows a hand holding a paper-like object, but no cup is visible, so the target relation cannot be assessed. Treat this as insufficient visual evidence (unknown), not as evidence that no progress occurred. The support traces appear to describe a different scene (paper over a cup); check that supports are bound to the same immutable snapshot and target before combining them. Preserve the distinction between absent (visible evidence of no progress), partial (visible progress), and unknown (required objects or their relation cannot be verified); do not infer absence from an unseen cup or from repeated, dependent observations. The aggregate matches the reference label, but that agreement does not establish the node’s visual reasoning as correct.

Make the node explicitly bind to the edited snapshot and the requested paper-into-cup relation, and require it to verify that both the paper and cup are visible before judging placement. Here the edited image shows a hand holding a blue paper-like object, but no cup is visible; that is unknown, not evidence of no progress. Preserve distinct outcomes for visible absence, visible partial progress, and insufficient evidence, rather than collapsing uncertainty into fail. Also verify that the dependent support uses the same snapshot and target: its confident “paper over a cup” description conflicts with the supplied edited image. Treat this as a binding/dependency consistency issue, not as negative visual evidence. The aggregate’s agreement with the reference label is not proof of sound reasoning; repeated dependent judgments and high confidence do not resolve the missing-object evidence."}
